_policy: Every consciously deferred piece of work gets a row: what was deferred, why, what enforcement exists meanwhile, and a review-by date. `cargo xtask deferrals --check` (weekly scheduled CI) fails once a row passes its date un-re-decided — a deferral nobody re-examines is a silent forever. Re-deciding means either building the thing (delete the row) or re-dating it with a fresh reason in the same commit. Decisions intended to be permanent do not belong here; they get ADRs.

deferrals.what: The pinned suite's auth/* client scenarios (OAuth metadata discovery, registration, PKCE flows) as host-SUT gates, which need a full OAuth client in the reference host. Re-decided 2026-10-13: review item 2.8, the half D4 (2026-09-24) brought in, is built — the authorization pages are in scope at both revisions, every MUST- and SHOULD-family keyword on them entered (AUTH-001..AUTH-085 at 2025-11-25, AUTH-086..AUTH-194 at 2026-07-28), and the clauses a recording can judge (the server's 401/403 WWW-Authenticate challenge: its scope, its error against the status, the insufficient_scope response's resource_metadata, and at 2026-07-28 offline_access and single-challenge) carry checks with corpus pairs. What remains deferred is only the host-as-SUT half D4 kept out
deferrals.why: A full OAuth client is a large build whose only consumer would be the host-as-SUT gate, and the trace validator cannot use it: the flow it would exercise runs between the client, the browser and the authorization server, off the MCP endpoint a recording captures (registry exclusions AUTH-* say clause by clause why). Making the exclusion permanent is an ADR, not a date; until one is written this row keeps the question on a clock
deferrals.meanwhile: The AUTH-* registry entries judge the HTTP-observable challenge clauses on every recorded session (corpus pairs under corpus/violations/auth-* and corpus/draft/violations/auth-*); TRAN-009 and TRAN-054 stay excluded and point at them; the four protocol client scenarios gate in CI

deferrals.what: The STABLE suite pin only — xtask's SUITE_VERSION (0.1.16, the 2025-11-25 gate) — bumps when a stable 0.2.0 exists, refreshing both expected-failures baselines and the agreement divergence ledger in the same change. The draft ratchet DRAFT_SUITE_VERSION is not deferred: it tracks the alpha dist-tag (0.2.0-alpha.12 since 2026-10-01). 03-conformance-strategy states the two pins' separate triggers
deferrals.why: Re-decided 2026-10-12, the review-by (2026-10-15) being due: there is still nothing stable to bump to. npm `latest` is 0.1.16, published 2026-03-30 and unchanged for six and a half months; `alpha` is 0.2.0-alpha.12 (2026-10-01). Re-fetched 2026-10-12 (register 2.4). Pin bumps are deliberate PRs with a scenario diff review (03-conformance-strategy §Official-suite version policy)
deferrals.meanwhile: The watch is a gate, not a date: `cargo xtask suite-currency` (weekly, in `claims-expire`) fails the moment npm's `latest` stops being 0.1.16, and a red weekly run files a tracking issue. The weekly suite-alpha job runs the alpha dist-tag non-blocking; the draft ratchet pins alpha.12 and gates every check's status; conformance#338's fix arrives with the stable bump and its agreement-divergence entry will go stale loudly
